edges.label: McCoy's shop produced the analysis Twining signed
edges.note: The AMC intelligence organisation under McCoy did the staff work behind the 23 September 1947 assessment; McCoy signed related AMC correspondence to the Chief of Staff two months later.

edges.label: The 1954 regulation was issued under Twining as Chief of Staff
edges.note: The officer who wrote in 1947 that the phenomenon was real was Air Force Chief of Staff when the regulation restricting public discussion of unexplained cases was promulgated.

edges.label: The AMC commander's 1947 assessment predates and undercuts the MOGUL account
edges.note: Twining wrote in September 1947 that the phenomenon was real while noting the lack of recovered exhibits; the Air Force's 1994 position requires that his own command's exploitation centre never connected the wave to a programme it was cleared for.

edges.label: Twining authored the founding 1947 assessment
edges.note: Lt. Gen. Twining signed 'AMC Opinion Concerning Flying Discs' on 23 September 1947 as commander of Air Materiel Command. The document survives in scanned form and is quoted in the Condon Report.

edges.label: Addressed to Schulgen at Air Force intelligence requirements
